**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part:** The entire cereal spike/head
- **Key visual features:**
  - The grain head is almost entirely replaced by dark, powdery/sooty masses of spores
  - A delicate, silvery-grey membrane is still partially encasing the dark spore masses
  - The spike rachis (central stem structure) remains visible
  - No normal grain development — all kernels converted to dark spore masses
  - Dark olive-brown to black coloration throughout the head

**Reasoning:**

This is a classic presentation of **Loose Smut**. The entire spike has been replaced by masses of dark fungal spores (teliospores) of *Ustilago nuda* (barley loose smut) or *Ustilago tritici* (wheat loose smut). The characteristic silvery-grey membrane that briefly encloses the spore mass before rupturing is still visible here. This distinguishes it from Dwarf Bunt (which shows intact, ball-shaped bunt balls with a fishy odor) and Head Scab/Fusarium (which shows pinkish discoloration on spikelets). The caption in the image explicitly confirms this identification.
